segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue mix
segmentRevenue.content:
Bayer reports three divisions: Crop Science (seeds, traits and crop protection, including glyphosate-based Roundup), Pharmaceuticals (prescription drugs such as Xarelto, Eylea and Nubeqa) and Consumer Health (OTC brands). Covestro (materials science/polyurethanes) was a fourth segment through FY2015, deconsolidated after its IPO/spin-off.

For Bayer: the 2018 Monsanto acquisition folded US seeds/traits into Crop Science and made it roughly half of group revenue, while Pharmaceuticals (ex-Xarelto/Eylea patent cliffs ahead) and Consumer Health have shrunk in relative share. The mix matters because the divisions have very different margin, litigation and cyclicality profiles.

What to watch:

  • Crop Science growth versus generic glyphosate competition and the US dicamba label vacatur
  • Pharmaceuticals revenue as Xarelto and Eylea face biosimilar/patent erosion
  • Whether Consumer Health is stabilising or still declining

litigation.title: Litigation special items vs EBIT
litigation.content:
Bayer has carried a multi-decade US mass-tort liability since the 2018 Monsanto acquisition: Roundup/glyphosate (alleged non-Hodgkin lymphoma link), PCB (polychlorinated biphenyl legacy contamination suits) and dicamba crop-damage claims. The litigation special charge is the amount deducted from EBIT each year to cover settlements, provisions and legal costs for these cases -- not already netted out of the EBIT bar shown here.

For Bayer: this is the single biggest swing factor in reported earnings. It peaked at roughly EUR13.2bn in FY2020 (initial Roundup provisioning), fell to as little as EUR0.2bn in FY2024, then jumped back to roughly EUR7.5bn in FY2025 as Bayer topped up provisions for a $7.25bn nationwide Roundup class settlement. On 2026-06-25 the US Supreme Court ruled 7-2 in Monsanto v. Durnell that FIFRA preempts state failure-to-warn claims -- a landmark de-risking win that, together with the class settlement and PCB resolutions, is central to the bull case that the litigation overhang is finally shrinking. The bear case notes the class settlement still needs final court approval, is contested by objectors, and new claims (e.g. Poe Hall) keep surfacing.

What to watch:

  • Whether annual litigation charges keep trending down after the FY2025 spike
  • Final court approval of the $7.25bn Roundup class settlement
  • Residual verdicts/appeals and any state-level legislative pushback against the Supreme Court's preemption ruling

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Bayer AG: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Bayer AG: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Bayer AG: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Bayer AG: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Bayer AG: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Bayer AG: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Bayer AG: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Bayer AG: operating income here already absorbs the Roundup/glyphosate, PCB and dicamba litigation special charges (see the litigation chart below) -- several billion euros in some years -- so a weak operating income year can be a litigation-provisioning year, not a trading one.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep, or a litigation charge)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Bayer AG: this is the sum of three divisions -- Crop Science, Pharmaceuticals and Consumer Health (see the segment mix chart below) -- so group growth can mask very different stories in each. Compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired (e.g. the 2018 Monsanto deal)
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Bayer AG: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
